newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mideast seen needing private infrastructure funds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast seen needing private infrastructure funds.

text.p: The Middle East and North Africa region needs $3 billion in private infrastructure investment a year to help it achieve economic growth targets, a World Bank official said on Wednesday.
Kemal Dervis, World Bank vice-president for the Middle East and North Africa, said the bank considered such investment as so essential that it was offering loans and risk guarantees.
Dervis, a speaker at the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) Economic Conference, also told reporters that the region was at a turning point in economic openness.
"I think we are at the turning point in terms of policy direction," he said. "There is a very good chance in the next two years we will see very large capital inflows."
Representatives from more than 90 countries are attending the three-day meeting which opened on Tuesday to discuss the region's investment climate and setting up joint ventures.

Economists see the Middle East and North Africa as among the last emerging markets. The region is eager to attract private investment but further easing of trade barriers and improvements to investment regulations are needed, they said.
Dervis said because of limited budgets, the public sector could no longer be expected to foot the entire bill for major projects, especially in water, ports, power, and roads.

"We need more private investment overall, in particular we need more private investment in infrastructure. Those investments are large and very risky," he said. "It will take an extra effort to attract private capital in those sectors. We are willing to come in and try to help reduce the level of risk."
He said such investment in the past two years averaged $200 million a year.

"One of the key instruments we're proposing to the private sector is not only World Bank loans to support this but guarantees," he said. "There is still a fairly high perception of risk -- foreign exchange convertibility, tariff policies, access to the power grid. Political risk and policy performance risk, we're willing to cover it."
Dervis said the $3 billion estimate was needed to achieve targeted overall average growth targets.
"About $3 billion a year in private investment in infrastructure is needed if an overall target of six percent average growth in the region is to be achieved," he said.

"That would allow, if you have population growth of 2.5 percent, per capita incomes to go up at 3.5 percent a year which would basically mean that in 15 years it would be close to double," he said. "It would lift MENA out of the poverty trap."
